profile.reading:
This record covers a TIM building on Via Lavisotto in the Campotrentino district on the northern edge of Trento, in the autonomous province of Trento in northern Italy. Its name, Centrale TIM Trento Nord, is the ordinary Italian description of a telephone exchange. Centrale is the standard word for an exchange building, and Trento Nord identifies which part of the city it serves. TIM, formerly Telecom Italia, is Italy's incumbent telephone operator and inherited several thousand such exchanges from the state monopoly era.

The physical evidence at the site fits an exchange. A freestanding TIM communication tower carrying mobile telephone equipment stands immediately beside the building and is separately recorded in the map data, which is the standard arrangement where a legacy exchange also hosts radio access equipment for the mobile network. Exchange buildings of this type contain switching and transmission plant, line terminations, batteries and rectifiers, and they are usually windowless, but they are not colocation data centres and they are not sold or measured as such.

TIM's own commercial data centre estate is operated under the Noovle brand, and the operator's published network page lists 16 certified data centres, in Turin, Milan, Padova, Bologna, Rome and Florence. No Trento facility appears on that list. That absence is the strongest published evidence available about this building, and it points the same way as the name.

The map history shows how the data centre classification arrived. The outline was drawn in March 2010 as a plain building and stayed that way for thirteen years. On 20 March 2023 a local mapper made two edits minutes apart. The first, commented in Italian as a building type change on Via Lavisotto, set building=data_center and telecom=data_center and named it Centrale Telecom Trento Nord. The second corrected the name to Centrale TIM Trento Nord and moved an existing tag recording TIM as the mobile telephone provider into the operator field. So the building was already known to the map as TIM mobile infrastructure before anyone called it a data centre, and the reclassification was one mapper's judgement rather than anything the operator published.

This registry records no floor area, no power figure of any kind, no certification and no operational status for this building, because TIM publishes none for it. What is established is the operator, the location and the building type.
